Surah al-Waqi'ah (The Inevitable Event) [Meccan, except verses 81 and 82, which are Medinan] [its verses are 96, 97, and 99]

﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs﴾ — the Resurrection (al-qiyamah) takes place.
﴿Nothing will deny its occurrence.﴾ [That is,] a soul that denies it, by negating it as it negated it in the worldly life (al-dunya).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah al-Waqi'ah (56), verse 3:

﴿Abasing [some], exalting [others]﴾. I.e., it (the Event) makes manifest the abasing of some peoples by their entry into the Fire, and the exalting of others by their entry into Paradise.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 56, verse 4:

﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ It is moved with an intense movement. "Idha" (when) here is a substitute (badal) for the first "idha" (when) in the preceding verse.
﴿And the mountains will be crumbled into powder﴾ — they will be broken into fine pieces.
﴿So they become scattered dust﴾ (ghubaran), ﴿dispersed﴾ (muntashiran).

[Qur'an 56:7] ﴿And you will be [in the Hereafter] ﴾ ... 

Wait, I should translate faithfully. Here is the translation:

﴿And you were﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿kinds﴾, categories.

ﷻ﴿So the companions of the right hand﴾: they are those who are given their records in their right hands. It is the subject (mubtada), and its predicate is ﴿what are the companions of the right hand?﴾, an expression of the greatness of their status through their entry into Paradise.

Translation:

﴿And the companions of the left hand﴾, that is, the left side, by which each of them will be given his record in his left hand. ﴿What are the companions of the left hand!﴾ This is a belittling of their state, because of their entry into the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 10:

﴿And the foremost [in faith and good deeds]﴾ to good, and they are the prophets. [It is] a subject (mubtada'); ﴿the foremost﴾ is an emphasis to magnify their rank.
﴿A multitude from the earlier generations﴾ is a *mubtada'* (the subject of a nominal sentence), meaning a group from the past nations.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 14:

﴿And a few from the later ones﴾ from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they are the foremost of the earlier nations and this community. And the predicate (khabar)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 15:

﴿Reclining upon couches woven together (mawdunah)﴾ woven with rods of gold and jewels.
Reclining on them, facing one another. These are two states (ḥāl, circumstantial accusatives) referring back to the pronoun in the predicate (al-khabar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 17:

﴿There will go round among them﴾ to serve them, ﴿eternal youths (wildan mukhalladun)﴾ in the form of children, who do not grow old.

With cups (aqdah) having no handles, and ewers (abariq) that have handles and spouts, and a cup (ka's), a vessel for drinking wine, from a flowing spring (ma'in), meaning wine flowing from a source that never ceases at all.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 56, verse 19:

﴿They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated.﴾ The verb يُنْزَفُونَ is read with a fatha on the zāy and also with a kasra, from the forms نَزَفَ الشّارِب (nazafa al-shārib) and أَنْزَفَ (anzafa), meaning that they will not lose their reason. It means that they will not suffer headache from it, nor loss of reason, unlike the khamr (wine) of this world.

﴿And the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire.﴾ (It is) for them, for enjoyment.

﴿And maidens⦆ women intensely black of the eyes and white of them, ﴿with wide, lovely eyes⦆ large-eyed women. Its plural form ʿīn has its ʿayn vowelled with kasra instead of ḍamma to harmonise with the yā' (ya), and its singular is ʿaynāʾ, like ḥamrāʾ. In another reading, ḥūr is read in the genitive (bi-jarr), as ḥūrin ʿīn.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 23:

﴿Like pearls well-guarded﴾ kept safe

﴿Jazā'﴾ is either an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu) or a verbal noun (maṣdar), with the understood governing verb being: "We made for them what has been mentioned as a recompense," or "We recompensed them."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 25:

﴿They hear therein﴾ in the Garden ﴿no vain talk﴾ obscene speech ﴿nor any sin﴾ anything that would be sinful.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 56, verse 26:

﴿Illā﴾ (but) [it is] ﴿qīlan﴾ (a saying), ﴿salāman salāman﴾ ("Peace, peace"), a substitute for ﴿qīlan﴾, for they hear it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 28:

﴿Among lote-trees﴾ the trees of the lote-tree (sidr, jujube) ﴿thornless﴾ having no thorns in them

[Qur'an 56:29] "And banana trees (ṭalḥ) arranged in layers (manḍūd)."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "﴿Ṭalḥ﴾ the banana tree (shajar al-mawz) ﴿manḍūd﴾ laden with fruit from its base up to its top."
﴿And shade extended﴾ perpetual.
﴿And water poured out﴾, flowing constantly.
﴿Neither cut off﴾ in time, ﴿nor forbidden﴾ by a price.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 34:

﴿And raised couches﴾ upon the thrones.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 35:

﴿Indeed, We have produced them with a special production.﴾ That is, the big-eyed maidens (al-Hur al-'In), created without birth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 36:

﴿We have made them virgins﴾ (ʿadhārā), every time their spouses come to them they find them virgins, and there is no pain.

﴿عُرُبًا﴾ (ʿuruban), with the ra vowelled either with a ḍamma or left sukūn, is the plural of ʿurūb, meaning those who are amorously devoted to their husband, out of love for him. ﴿أتْرابًا﴾ (atraban) is the plural of tirb, meaning equal in age.

﴿For the companions of the right hand﴾ is a ṣila (a grammatical complement, a phrase that is attached to a preceding word) of أنشأناهن (*anshaʾnāhunna*, "We created them") or جعلناهن (*jaʿalnāhunna*, "We made them"), and they are: ﴿a host from the earlier generations, and a host from the later ones﴾.
In scorching wind (samum), a hot wind from the Fire that penetrates the pores, and boiling water (hamim), water of intense heat.
﴿And a shade of black smoke⁠﴾ — a smoke intensely black.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 44:

﴿Neither cool⁠﴾ like other shades, ﴿nor pleasant⁠﴾ in appearance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 45:

﴿Indeed, they had been before that[, in the world,] affluent (mutrafin)﴾ [in the world,] ﴿affluent﴾, pampered (mu'annamin), who would not exert themselves in obedience.
﴿And they used to persist in the great violation﴾ the sin, ﴿the great﴾ i.e., polytheism (shirk).

﴿They used to say, "When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again?"﴾ Regarding the two hamzahs (الهَمْزَتَيْنِ) in the two places: al-tahqiq (التَّحْقِيق, pronouncing the hamzah in full) and tashil al-thaniyah (تَسْهِيل الثّانِيَة, softening the second hamzah into a sound between hamzah and alif), and idkhal alif baynahuma (إدْخال ألِف بَيْنهما, inserting an alif between the two), in both manners of recitation.

﴿Or our forefathers of old?﴾ With the waw vowelled with a fatha, for coordination (ʿaṭf), and the hamza for interrogation (istifhām). It, in this and in what precedes it, is for expressing astonishment or disbelief (istibʿād). In another recitation, with the waw sukūn, it is coordination with ʾaw (or), and the thing coordinated upon (al-maʿṭūf ʿalayhi) is the place (maḥall) of inna and its noun (ismuhā).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 50:

﴿Indeed, you will surely be gathered to an appointed time﴾ (lil-waqt), the time of ﴿a known Day﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection.

Verse 52 of Surah al-Waqi'ah (56): ﴿Indeed, you will be eating from a tree of zaqqum﴾. This clarifies "the tree."

Note on the translation: the Arabic gloss here is the Jalalayn's explanatory phrase, "بَيان لِلشَّجَرِ," which means it specifies or clarifies what "the tree" (al-shajar) refers to, so I've rendered it that way.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 53:**

﴿Then you will fill your bellies from it﴾ from the tree
﴿Then you will drink on it﴾, i.e., the zaqqum that is eaten.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 55:

﴿Then you will drink, drinking﴾ with the shin vowelled with a fatha or a damma, being a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿Like the thirsty camels﴾ — al-hīm (الهِيم) is the plural of haymān for the masculine and haymā for the feminine, like ʿaṭshān and ʿaṭshā (thirsty).
﴿هَذا نُزُلهمْ﴾ That is their provision: what has been prepared for them ﴿يَوْم الدِّين﴾ on the Day of Recompense, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 57:

﴿We created you﴾ (ﷻ), We brought you into being from non-existence, ﴿why then will you not believe﴾ (hallā, meaning "why not") ﴿in the Resurrection﴾, since He who is able to originate is able to restore.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 56, verse 58:

﴿Have you considered that which you emit?﴾ (i.e., you pour out) of the semen into the wombs of women.

﴿Are you﴾ [pronounced with] the two hamzas fully articulated (*tahqiq*), the second changed into an alif, and also eased (*tashil*), with an alif inserted between the eased hamza and the other one, and with that alif omitted in the other positions. ﴿Create it﴾, i.e., the seed (*al-maniyy*), into a human being (*basharan*).

We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone (بِمَسْبُوقِينَ, bi-masbuqin, "outpaced" or "overcome"), ﴿We have decreed⁠﻿—﻿﻿ ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—…

Let me give the translation cleanly:

Qur'an 56:60 is rendered: ﴿We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "﴿Nahnu qaddarna﴾ (We have decreed), with the doubled letter (bil-tashdid) and without it (bil-takhfif), ﴿death among you, and We are not to be outpaced﴾, i.e., not incapable (بِعاجِزِينَ, bi-'ajizin)."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 61:

﴿عَلى﴾ meaning عَنْ (on, in the sense of "concerning" or "in respect of"). ﴿أنْ نُبَدِّل﴾ meaning نَجْعَل (to make). ﴿أمْثالكُمْ﴾ meaning مَكانكُمْ (in your place). ﴿ونُنْشِئكُمْ﴾ meaning نَخْلُقكُمْ (and create you). ﴿فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ meaning مِن الصُّوَر (in forms), such as كالقِرَدَةِ (the apes) والخَنازِير (and the swine), which you do not know.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾. And in one reading, with the sukun on the شِين (shin), it is read ﴿النَّشْأَة﴾ (al-nash'ah). ﴿So why do you not remember?﴾ In it there is idgham (assimilation) of the second تَاء (tā') which originally was in the root, into the ذَال (dhāl).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 63:

﴿Have you considered what you plant?﴾ You stir up the earth and cast the seed into it.
﴿Is it you who cultivate it?﴾ — you cause it to grow.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 65:

﴿If We willed, We would make it debris﴾ dry vegetation with no grain in it. ﴿Then you would be left⁠ (fazaltum)﴾ its original form was ẓaliltum, with the lam vowelled with a kasra, and one lam was dropped for lightness; meaning, you would remain by day ﴿jesting⁠ (tafakkahūn)﴾ from it one of the two tā' was dropped; originally it means you would be astonished at that and say:
﴿Indeed, we are burdened with debt﴾: the expense of our sowing.
﴿Rather, we have been deprived﴾ prevented from our provision.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 69:

﴿Is it you who sent it down from the rain clouds?﴾ The clouds (al-muzn), plural of muzna (a single cloud).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 70:

﴿Had We willed, We could have made it bitter (ujaj)﴾, salty, its drinking impossible. ﴿Why then do you not give thanks?﴾ Why not (halla)?

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 56, verse 71:

﴿Have you considered the fire that you kindle?﴾ (You) bring it out from the green tree.
﴿Is it you who produced its tree?﴾ Like the markh, the 'afar, and the kalkh (trees whose wood was rubbed together to make fire).

﴿We have made it a reminder﴾ of the Fire of Hell, ﴿and a provision﴾ for sustenance, ﴿for the travellers﴾, i.e., for the travellers, from "aqwa al-qawm" (they became destitute of provisions), meaning they became in the *qawa* (with *al-qasr* and *al-madd*, i.e., *al-qafr*), which is a desert with no vegetation or water.
﴿So glorify﴾ declare Him free of any imperfection ﴿in the name of﴾ the particle بِ (bi) is extra (zāʾida, grammatically superfluous) ﴿your Lord, the Mighty﴾ Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 75:

﴿Fa-lā uqsimu﴾ [the "lā" here is extra (zāʾida)] ﴿bi-mawāqiʿ al-nujūm﴾ [by the places where the stars fall, i.e., their setting-places (bi-masāqitihā li-ghurūbihā)]

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 56, verse 76:

﴿And indeed it﴾ (i.e., the oath by them) ﴿is indeed a great oath, if only you knew﴾. (That is,) if you were among those possessing knowledge, you would know the greatness of this oath.
﴿Indeed, it﴾: i.e., the one recited to you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 78:

﴿In a Book﴾ written, ﴿well-guarded﴾ protected, and it is the Mushaf.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 79:

﴿None touches it﴾ is a statement (khabar) in the sense of a prohibition (nahy), ﴿except the purified﴾, those who have purified themselves from the ritual impurities (ahdath).
﴿A revelation﴾ sent down.
﴿Are you then of this discourse﴾ the Qur'an ﴿disdainful?﴾ — neglecting it, denying it.

﴿And you make your provision﴾ from the rain, meaning its thanks, ﴿that you deny﴾ Allah's giving of water, when you say, "We were given rain by such-and-such a star" (*nawʾ*, the rising or setting of a lunar mansion).

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on Surah 56, verse 83:

﴿Then why not﴾ (fa-lawlā), meaning fa-hallā (why not?), ﴿when it [the soul] reaches﴾ (idhā balaghat), meaning the soul (al-rūḥ) reaches, at the time of death-throes (al-naz'), ﴿the throat﴾ (al-ḥulqūm), which is the passage of food (majrā al-ṭaʿām).
"And you," O attendants of the dying person, ﴿at that time are looking on﴾, looking at him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 85:

﴿And We are nearer to him than you are﴾ by knowledge, ﴿but you do not see﴾ from al-basirah (insight), i.e., you do not know that.
﴿Then why not﴾ (i.e., فَهَلّا, "why do you not"), ﴿if you are not to be recompensed﴾, meaning not to be requited, that is, that you will not be resurrected, according to your claim.

ﷺ is not present here, so no honorific needed. Translating the passage:

﴿Why do you not return it﴾ — you return the soul to the body after it has reached the throat — ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in what you claim. Then "why not" (falawla) is an emphatic repetition of the first ("why not" in the earlier verse). "When" (idha) is an adverb of time governing "you return" (tarji'un), to which both conditions are attached. The meaning is: why do you not return it, if you deny resurrection and are truthful in your denial, so that death is removed from its place just as resurrection is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 88:

﴿Then if he was﴾ among the dead

Then there is rest (fa-rawh), i.e., he has repose, and provision (rayhan), i.e., good sustenance, and a Garden of bliss.

Is the response (jawab) to "amma" or to "in" or to both? There are opinions.

Translation:

﴿So, peace be upon you﴾ meaning: he has safety from the punishment ﴿from the companions of the right﴾, in that he is one of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 56, verse 95:

﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty.﴾ It is an idafa (construct phrase) of the qualified noun to its attribute: "حق اليقين" (haqq al-yaqin) is "the certainty that is true," where "حق" (haqq) describes "اليقين" (al-yaqin). The qualified noun (al-mawsuf) is "اليقين," and its attribute (al-sifa) is "حق."
﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent﴾ (already passed)
